column1: # Install-verification matrix. Tab-separated. Columns:
#   name        unique row label (also the results/<name>.log basename)
#   image       Docker base image (a pristine, official distro — nothing pre-baked)
#   platform    linux/arm64 or linux/amd64 (both run on native CI runners)
#   expect      pass | pass-managed-python
#   python      stock | none
# expect semantics:
#   pass                installer succeeds, deps resolve, Chalie boots, and every
#                       runtime probe passes (readiness, webserver, chromium,
#                       voice round trip, deno)
#   pass-managed-python everything `pass` requires, plus one more assertion: the
#                       venv was built from a uv-managed CPython 3.12 under
#                       ~/.local/share/uv/python. The installer prefers a stock
#                       python3 whenever one is 3.11+, and only when the host has
#                       none does it install a managed CPython of its own — these
#                       rows are the hosts where that second path is the one taken
# python semantics — what the harness sets up BEFORE running the installer:
#   stock  install the distro's own python3 first. Official base images are more
#          stripped than a real machine (the Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora bases ship
#          no python3 at all), so this reproduces a realistic system
#   none   leave the host with no python3 whatsoever
# Every row is a SUPPORTED platform. install.sh handles exactly two Linux
# families — apt (Debian/Ubuntu) and dnf (Fedora/RHEL) — plus macOS on Apple
# Silicon; anything else the installer now refuses outright, so there is nothing
# to verify. Adding a row means committing to support that platform.
